To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnitude of the overfeeding-induced weight gain is a key predictor of metabolic risk, and that the relative expansion of subcutaneous adipose vs visceral adipose tissue is an important determinant of the metabolic health of individuals.
overfeeding studies, in which we imposed short-term positive energy imbalance, helped unravel the cellular, metabolic and behavioural adaptations to energy excess.

the magnitude of weight gained and its metabolic consequences are highly variable between individuals, with the magnitude of weight change and the degree of metabolic disturbance both being determined by a combination of genetic, physiological and environmental factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biological mechanisms underpinning the development of obesity and related metabolic complications.
the cellular, physiological, behavioural and genetic factors that underpin the heterogeneity in the human response to nutrient excess
the cellular and physiological mechanisms that underlie the heterogeneity in the response to overfeeding and the implications for the metabolic health consequences of excess nutrient intake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a lot we don’t yet know.
the overfeeding studies have provided invaluable insights into the mechanisms underlying adipose tissue expansion, susceptibility to weight gain and the associated metabolic complications.
the human overfeeding studies have taught us that the response to overfeeding is highly variable, but that there are common themes in the response to overnutrition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adipose tissue expansion is a complex process involving both adipocyte number and size.
adipose tissue expansion is not a passive process, but is governed by biological responses to nutrient excess, which are modulated by intrinsic/extrinsic factors.
the extent of adipose tissue expansion with nutrient excess and metabolic response is determined by intrinsic and extrinsic factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biological responses of SAT to nutrient excess are highly individualised.
the magnitude of overfeeding response is heterogeneous, and the extent of weight gain and metabolic response are influenced by a number of intrinsic/extrinsic factors.
the magnitude and pattern of overfeeding responses (weight gain, body composition, SAT remodelling, metabolic responses) is highly individualised.
